args.text: [lane-plover] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System, the internet's address book) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to an old server after a site moves or fails over, so they see errors or outages. (2) Slow recovery: fixes to records, such as changing a faulty address, take longer to reach everyone. (3) Prolonged poisoning: if a forged answer is cached, it stays in place and misdirects users until it expires.

[lane-plover] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a client often cannot tell whether a request was lost or merely answered slowly. If repeating a request has the same effect as sending it once, the client can safely try again without, for example, charging a customer twice or creating duplicate orders.

[lane-plover] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) Time leakage: the leading bits encode the creation time in UTC, so anyone seeing an identifier can estimate when a record was made, and that may be sensitive. (2) Size and ordering limits: it takes 16 bytes, which is larger than a plain integer key and so makes indexes bigger, and IDs created within the same millisecond on different machines are only roughly ordered, not strictly.

[lane-plover] A write-ahead log (WAL) is a file where a database records each change before applying it to the main data, so nothing is lost if the system crashes part-way through. After a crash, the database replays the log to restore a consistent state, and writing the log in order is also quicker than updating scattered data pages.

[lane-plover] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a client update can change speed through new defaults, retry rules or connection handling, so an unpinned version could make results look better or worse when the system under test has not changed. (2) Repeatability: others, or you at a later date, can only rerun the test and get comparable results if they know exactly which client was used.
